segments.title: 第70章 想得美
segments.content:
Reigniting the Verdant Era Chapter 70: Dream On

In the evening, inside the classroom dedicated to the Literature Club.

Xu Youyu walked into the classroom yawning, casually found a chair and sat down, then looked at the other two people in the room.

One was the president of the Literature Club, Duan Qintian from Class One of the third year.

The other was Qin Yawei, who was a vice president just like her.

"The matter of setting up a booth for club recruitment, wasn't that all settled at noon?" Xu Youyu asked with a curious look after sitting down. "Is there something else? I have Student Council matters to attend to later."

"It's like this." Duan Qintian knew Xu Youyu was the vice president of the Student Council, so he pulled out three lists from his pocket and cut to the chase. "Teacher Kong gave us a list of students who got full marks on the high school entrance exam essay or have won city-level or above writing competition awards. There are 37 people in total."

"The teacher's meaning is, she recommends we proactively recruit them."

"The other club members have gone to get busy with setting up the recruitment booth, so I was thinking, why don't we split these 37 people among us?"

"Sure," Xu Youyu nodded.

Qin Yawei, who was at the side, also nodded and took a list from Duan Qintian.

"One for each of you. The ones with checkmarks are the people you're responsible for," Duan Qintian said. "I'm responsible for 13, you two get 12 each."

"There's no need to rush this. The club recruitment will last for several days."

"After today's recruitment ends, if there are still people on the list who haven't signed up, we'll go find them."

"Okay." Xu Youyu didn't look closely at the list and stuffed it directly into her hand, then left in a hurry. "The Student Council has a meeting, so I'll be going."

Watching Xu Youyu's retreating figure, Qin Yawei, who was at the side, pouted. "If she knew the Student Council would be so busy, she shouldn't have run for vice president in the first place."

"Xu Youyu has won awards in competitions," Duan Qintian said with a laugh. "And the election was fair and impartial, so there's nothing to complain about."

"Her dad is a literature professor at Qianjiang University. Winning an award isn't exactly hard for her," Qin Yawei said disdainfully. "Besides, during the election, a lot of the votes for her came from boys. You think I don't know what you guys are thinking? It's just because she has big boobs."

"Hey, hey, hey." Duan Qintian looked helpless. "How can you say something like that to me? Have you no shame?"

"I'm just speaking the truth," Qin Yawei huffed. "You dare say you weren't looking just now? You secretly glanced at least three times."

"...I can't be bothered to argue with you." Duan Qintian stood up and walked out of the classroom, unable to stand her. "Anyway, just remember to invite the people on the list."

"Hmph." Qin Yawei snorted in dissatisfaction, then glanced at the check-marked names on her list.

Du Juncong, Tan Na, Zou Xue... Li Luo.

After math class in the afternoon was history.

When Li Luo returned from Teacher Kong's office, he first put the poster up on the blackboard.

Since some of his classmates were in the hallway and others had gone to the restroom, not everyone was present, so he didn't rush to make the announcement.

Only after the next history class ended did Li Luo walk up to the podium and explain the club recruitment to everyone.

"In short, if any students in our class plan to participate in competitions, you can go check out the various subject-specific competition clubs."

"If you don't have that in mind, you can also join some of the other interest-based clubs."

"Isn't there a Chinese Language Club?" Hua Xiuxiu had looked at the poster earlier and couldn't find it. "There's only a Literature Club. Is that the competition club for Chinese?"

"Chinese is a bit special," Li Luo explained. "Generally, only the writing competitions hold any weight. Other Chinese knowledge competitions are pretty average, so there's only a Literature Club."

"Oh." Hua Xiuxiu nodded. As a girl who loved literature, she was clearly quite interested in the Literature Club.

"Then what are the requirements to join the Literature Club, Class President?" Lin Yuan raised his hand to ask on Hua Xiuxiu's behalf.

"You'll have to ask them yourselves." Li Luo pointed out the window toward Houde Road. "Anyway, every club will have its own booth, and they'll explain the joining requirements there."

"Our next class is PE. After class, we can directly secure a good spot. The booths are right outside the sports field."

"If there are any clubs you're interested in, you can just ask them directly then."

After making the announcement, Li Luo walked off the podium and returned to his seat, then glanced at Yan Zhusheng. "Which club do you plan to join?"

"I want to check out the Rock Music Club. I'm not really interested in the others," Yan Zhusheng said without hesitation, then turned to look at him. "Are you going?"

"I haven't decided yet," Li Luo said, shaking his head. "I'll take a look first when the time comes."

"Class President, let's go to the Basketball Club," Zhu Yufei at the side said with a grin. "That way, we can find people from the club to play ball with in the evenings and on Saturdays."

"That's not a bad idea," Li Luo nodded.

"Not going to the Anime Club?" Zhang Guohuang suggested in a secretive whisper. "I've asked around. The Anime Club sometimes holds small cosplay exhibitions. Don't you guys want to see that?"

"Come play basketball with me." Zhu Yufei slung an arm around Zhang Guohuang's neck. "What's so fun about the Anime Club?"

"Aren't you going to join the Literature Club?" Hua Xiuxiu also came over upon hearing the conversation and asked Li Luo, "You got a full score on your entrance exam essay. Getting into the Literature Club should be a breeze for you."

"Forget about the Literature Club." Li Luo shook his head. "I heard you have to submit at least one manuscript every month. I don't have that kind of free time."

He already had to squeeze in time at night to write. Who would want to contribute manuscripts to the school's Literature Club?

It's not like they paid for it.

"The Literature Club prints a monthly journal that includes all the members' works for that month, and it's circulated around the school," Hua Xiuxiu reminded him. "Don't you want more students to see your work?"

"Uhh..." Hearing Hua Xiuxiu say this, Li Luo shook his head even more forcefully. "No, not at all!"

He'd be thrilled if Zhu Yufei, Zhang Guohuang, and the others didn't read it. If his pen name was ever exposed, he couldn't imagine how weirdly this bunch, who had read the novel, would look at him, their class president.

Besides, these guys didn't have much money in their pockets and read pirated versions of web novels. Li Luo couldn't earn any subscription fees from them.

It's best if these guys just focus on their studies!

Seeing that Li Luo really didn't want to join, Hua Xiuxiu shook her head and gave up. She was originally going to ask if he wanted to go check out the Literature Club's booth together later.

"Xiuxiu, I'm actually quite interested in the Literature Club," Lin Yuan popped out from the side and said. "Wanna go together later?"

"Sure." Hua Xiuxiu nodded. "But Chinese composition has never been your strong suit. Why do you want to join the Literature Club?"

"You have to strengthen your weaknesses," Lin Yuan said righteously. "Wait for me after PE class."

"Lin Yuan, aren't you going to check out the Basketball Club with us?" Zhu Yufei couldn't help but ask.

"Ahem." Lin Yuan coughed twice and leaned over to whisper, "You guys go first. I'll find you after I'm done with the Literature Club."

"Let's go. Time for class," Li Luo said.

And so, the group walked outside, heading to the sports field for PE class.

But just as they stepped out the door, Li Luo came face to face with Ying Chanxi, who was coming downstairs.

Li Luo told the others to go on ahead and looked at Ying Chanxi, asking, "What's up?"

"Your next class is PE, right?" Ying Chanxi asked. "How about we go eat first after class, and then walk around the booths on Houde Road?"

Earlier that morning, Ying Chanxi had Li Luo copy Class Eight's schedule for her, so she came down to find him before PE class to discuss getting food and the club recruitment fair.

"What club are you going to join?" Li Luo asked curiously.

"Umm..." When it came to this topic, Ying Chanxi felt a bit of a headache. "Teacher Sun wants me to join the Math Club, but the physics and chemistry teachers also want me to join their clubs, so I don't know which one to choose."

"...Aren't there any more entertaining options?"

"There are," Ying Chanxi nodded. "The Literature Club is actually okay too. It's relatively relaxed, so it can be chosen along with competition clubs for other subjects. Want to join together?"

The corner of Li Luo's mouth twitched, and he felt a little reluctant to answer.

"...How about the Anime Club instead? I'd rather see you in a cosplay outfit."

"What are you talking about? Dream on!"

(End of Chapter)
